title: Every Executive Sheet item must appear in the Executive Document, but derived actions may be filtered out for clarity
content:
Two provisions set the scope of the disclosure obligation precisely. A.1.10.2.4.8.3.7: "The Core Facilitator must ensure that **every item** from the Executive Sheet is included in the details section of the Executive Document," presented "in order of judged impact/importance." A.1.10.2.4.8.2.5, on derived actions: "Derived actions that are overly technical, redundant, or irrelevant to the proposal's primary focus **may be excluded** to maintain clarity and accessibility."

So the guarantee to voters is that nothing in the Spell happens without a corresponding announced input action — but not that every mechanical consequence is enumerated. Completeness is promised at the level of intent; detail below that is editorial.

That is a coherent line: input actions are what a voter decides about, derived actions are how they are implemented, and the implementation layer is verified by parties equipped to check it (Technical Point, Content Liaisons, Spell Reviewers). It is also the place where the framework is most exposed, since "overly technical" is judged by the same party writing the document, and a consequential derived action could be filtered out under a clarity rationale.

A.1.10.2.4.8.3.1 constrains the discretion from the other side: "the technical information in the Executive Sheet must be identical to the Executive Document." What is included must match exactly; only what may be omitted is discretionary.

The consistency rule is notably bidirectional — "if the order of items in the Executive Document differs from the Executive Sheet, the Executive Sheet must be updated to match." The voter-facing ordering wins, and the internal working artifact is corrected to it, which is unusual for a document derived from another.
description: Completeness binds at the input-action level; A.1.10.2.4.8.2.5 lets overly technical, redundant or irrelevant derived actions be omitted from the voter-facing document.
